mission: Ben has returned to Shedu Maad after Iresh. This is the first in-person conversation between Ben and Luke since the holo calls. Luke asks about the holocron. Ben says it is gone, then clarifies only that it is somewhere it cannot hurt anyone. Luke senses the incompleteness and does not force the answer. Ben privately justifies learning what he needs before disposing of it. He is not lying. He is not telling the truth either. Thread Ben’s self-definition here: he is beginning to understand that being a good Jedi does not mean becoming a mirror image of Luke, and surviving Jacen does not mean pretending Jacen taught him nothing. He keeps his voice steady, but his hand tightens around the edge of the table as he answers. Recommended exchange: Luke: The holocron? Ben: Gone. Luke: Gone where? Ben: Somewhere it can’t hurt anyone. Luke: That wasn’t what I asked. Ben: I know.
why_now: Ben has been back at Shedu Maad for hours and has put off this conversation long enough. Luke has not called him in or demanded a report. He is simply present, and Ben has to go to him.
conflict: Ben is not lying — 'somewhere it can't hurt anyone' is technically true — but the omission is real and Luke senses it, and neither of them forces the other to name what is actually happening. The most painful version of Luke being emotionally intelligent is that he does not ask the question he already knows the answer to.
turning_point: Luke senses the incompleteness but does not force the answer.
closing_hook: Luke senses the incompleteness but does not force the answer.
setting: Shedu Maad, Luke's personal quarters at the Jedi compound — evening, dimmed Hapan recycler-tang in the air. Luke at the window. A table Luke built himself during the quiet months after Crucible occupies the center of the sitting room. Ben sits across it from his father. The holocron stays in Ben's belt pouch through the entire conversation. The room is the most intimate space in the book.
emotional_trajectory: Luke is not fooled. Ben is not villainous. The danger is the defensible omission. Ben is young and frightened and morally compromised at the same time. The words taste like something he will have to live with.

stakes.personal: Ben has prepared a version of the truth that is technically defensible and knows it will not be enough. His hand is going to tighten on the table edge when he says it. He knows that too. He will say it anyway, because the alternative — explaining what he is actually doing with the holocron — is not something he is ready to say to Luke yet, maybe ever.
stakes.interpersonal: Luke's post-Crucible quietness makes the silence between them load-bearing. He is not pressing. He is not performing patience. He is genuinely still, the way he has been since the Mortis-adjacent encounter — further away even when he is looking directly at Ben — and Ben notices and does not ask about it, and Luke notices that Ben notices and does not ask.
stakes.external: The omission will not be a secret forever. The holocron is in Ben's quarters. Luke senses the answer is incomplete. The case is resolved and the dangerous knowledge is unresolved, and both of them are leaving the conversation with that fact between them.

sensory_details: Luke's quarters at Shedu Maad: Hapan recycler-tang in the evening air, the table Luke built himself during the quiet months after Crucible — solid, hand-worked, imperfect in the way that means someone spent real time on it. Luke is at the window when Ben arrives. The room is the most intimate space in the book and the most exposed.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Luke asks about the holocron: 'The holocron?' Ben answers: 'Gone.' Luke: 'Gone where?' Ben: 'Somewhere it can't hurt anyone.' Luke: 'That wasn't what I asked.' Ben: 'I know.' — and then silence. Ben's hand has tightened on the table edge. Luke has seen it.
turning_point_detail.shift: Luke does not force the answer. He lets the silence be what it is. Ben feels the incompleteness of his own answer from inside it — not shame exactly, but the specific weight of saying something technically true and knowing that is not the same as being honest.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben leaves Luke's quarters with the conversation ended but not resolved. Luke knows. Ben knows Luke knows. The words taste like something he will have to live with.

emotional_arc.start: Ben arrives at Luke's quarters with a prepared answer and a tightness in his chest that he is mistaking for professionalism. He has done the work. He has a defensible position. He will say it cleanly.
emotional_arc.shift: The exchange is exactly as short as Ben prepared for, and it lands exactly wrong — not because Luke confronts him, but because Luke's quiet acceptance of the incomplete answer is harder to bear than accusation would be.
emotional_arc.end: Ben is twenty-one and morally compromised and not a villain and not fully honest, and the conversation is over, and he will carry the weight of this answer for a long time. He is beginning to understand that this is what his most dangerous choices cost: they taste defensible all the way down.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben enters Luke's quarters and the distance of all the holo calls collapses into a single small room — first in-person conversation since before Iresh.
key_beats.state_change: The managed distance of remote reporting is gone; Ben has to be in the room with his father and the container in his belt.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the room being smaller than prepared for; the container's weight making itself known before Luke has spoken

key_beats.beat_description: Luke asks quiet questions about the Foundation, Aevyn, Tess, and the Iresh operation; Ben answers fully — everything except the container.
key_beats.state_change: The factual record of the case is complete; the one omission is specific and deliberate.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the practiced fluency of a truthful account; the omission managed by not getting near its edge

key_beats.beat_description: Luke asks about the holocron; the exchange lands exactly as Ben prepared and exactly wrong at the same time.
key_beats.state_change: Ben's prepared answer — technically true, incomplete — is delivered; Luke hears what it is not.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the hand tightening on the table edge before the words are finished; the awareness that Luke has seen it

key_beats.beat_description: Luke does not force the answer; Ben does not offer it; the silence between them is load-bearing.
key_beats.state_change: Neither of them names what is actually in the room — the choice belongs to Ben, and Luke does not take it from him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the silence heavier than accusation would be; the specific weight of being trusted with a decision he is not sure he deserves

key_beats.beat_description: Ben leaves with the conversation ended but not resolved; Luke senses the incompleteness and does not call him back.
key_beats.state_change: The omission is established as a fact between them — not hidden from Luke, not acknowledged, just present.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the words tasting defensible all the way down; the knowledge that this is what his most dangerous choices cost
